stand: Sudan's army (SAF) and the RSF remain at war into a fourth year. Army chief Burhan has rejected negotiations, vowing to retake all RSF-held territory, as fighting intensifies in North and West Kordofan and the RSF kills civilians near En Nahud. The US and Egypt continue pressing for a Sudanese-led dialogue toward civilian rule, saying neither side represents legitimate governance. WHO warns health needs in Darfur, especially Tawila's 700,000 displaced, far exceed resources, with its 2026 appeal only 23% funded, as refugee outflow into South Sudan tops 1.4 million.

claims.text: UN Human Rights Council adopted a resolution demanding an immediate, unconditional ceasefire in Sudan and extended its fact-finding mission.
claims.by: Says: UN Human Rights Council (28-10-9 vote, Geneva). Denies: Sudan urged member states to reject the resolution.

claims.text: RSF's siege and capture of el-Fasher, North Darfur, bore the hallmarks of genocide.
claims.by: Says: UN-mandated independent international fact-finding mission for Sudan.

claims.text: An air strike killed a WFP driver on a convoy travelling between Dilling and Kadugli, South Kordofan.
claims.by: Says: World Food Programme. No party claimed responsibility.

claims.text: Both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the RSF are carrying out indiscriminate aerial bombardments and drone strikes on civilians.
Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan jointly backed Sudan's army-led government and rejected the RSF's parallel administration.
claims.by: Says: joint statement of the four leaders (Sisi, Afwerki, Mohamud, Burhan).

claims.text: The US is pushing for a regional agreement on an immediate humanitarian truce, including troop withdrawals and safe corridors.
claims.by: Says: White House senior adviser Massad Boulos and Trump administration officials.

claims.text: Sudan accuses Washington of denying army chief Burhan a visa to attend the UN General Assembly.
claims.by: Says: Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salim Ahmed Ibrahim. Response: US State Department declined to comment.

claims.text: The RSF's rival "Tasis" government named a Dutch-Sudanese lawyer, Osama Said, as its Justice Minister in early May 2026.
claims.by: Says: Osama Said confirms his nomination; says he has not yet formally accepted the post.

claims.text: The UN Security Council called the RSF's "Tasis" parallel government a direct danger to Sudan's territorial integrity when it was founded.
RSF commander Algoney Dagalo, brother of RSF leader Hemedti, attended a Hague peace conference under a false name while under US sanctions; he is now also EU-sanctioned and barred from entry.
claims.by: Says: Dutch foreign ministry and conference organiser The Hague Peace Projects confirm his presence and the false name.

claims.text: Famine has been confirmed multiple times over the past two years in parts of Sudan, with other areas still at risk.
claims.by: Says: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC).

claims.text: Al-Burhan vowed to continue fighting until the RSF is removed from Sudan, rejecting negotiations to end the war.
claims.by: Says: Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan (quoted via Sudan News Agency).

claims.text: The RSF killed 10 civilians and wounded others in an attack on Abu Ajal village, West Kordofan.
claims.by: Says: Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, a local charity group.

claims.text: More than 5,500 people were displaced from Blue Nile state villages over three days amid deteriorating security.
Neither the Sudanese Armed Forces nor the RSF, nor their leaders, represent legitimate constitutional governance for Sudan.
Sudan's army advanced toward En Nahud and Al Khuway in West Kordofan after gains in North Kordofan, as the RSF massed in the area.
Since fighting began in April 2023, 221 health workers have been killed, 16 kidnapped and 142 arrested across Sudan.
Drone strikes damaging health facilities in Sudan surged 88% in the first eight months of 2026, rising from 16 cases in 2025 to 30.
Two-thirds of drone strikes damaging health facilities were attributed to the RSF, with Kordofan particularly affected.
SAF drone strikes also increasingly damaged health facilities between January and April 2026, mostly in Darfur and Kordofan.

Health and humanitarian needs in Darfur, particularly Tawila, where more than 700,000 displaced people face severe gaps in health, nutrition, food, water, sanitation and protection, far exceed available resources.
Darfur hosts 65% of Sudan's 8.6 million internally displaced people.
WHO's $97.7 million humanitarian appeal for Sudan in 2026 is only 23% funded.
Rising malnutrition is a major concern at Darfur health facilities, expected to worsen amid poor rainfall, crop failures and a strong El Niño event.
claims.by: Says: WHO Representative in Sudan Dr Abdinasir Abubakar.

claims.text: Sudan's national food costs rose 16% in August, driven by sharp increases in vegetable oil, goat meat and cow meat prices.

timeline.text: WHO Representative Dr Abdinasir Abubakar completes a 10-day mission across Darfur states to assess health needs.
Insecurity Insight tallies 794 health-care attack incidents in Sudan since April 2023, with drone strikes on facilities up 88% in 2026.
A WFP vehicle hits an explosive device in Dilling after a food distribution run.
An air strike kills a WFP driver on a convoy between Dilling and Kadugli, South Kordofan.
Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan hold a four-way summit in New Alamein, backing Sudan's army-led government.
US envoy Massad Boulos meets Sudanese army chief Burhan at a luncheon hosted by Egypt's Sisi, on the AU meeting sidelines.
Qatar Red Crescent Society launches a medical convoy at Bahri Teaching Hospital, Khartoum.
UN Human Rights Council adopts resolution demanding a ceasefire and extending the Sudan fact-finding mission's mandate.
Al-Burhan tells a rally in Village 5, Merowe he will retake all RSF territory and rejects negotiations.
RSF kills 10 civilians in Abu Ajal village, West Kordofan, says Dar Hamar Emergency Committee.
IOM reports more than 5,500 people displaced from Blue Nile villages over three days amid deteriorating security.
Sudan's army advances on En Nahud and Al Khuway in West Kordofan as the RSF masses nearby.
WHO calls for urgent increase in resources and unhindered humanitarian access to meet Darfur's health needs.
RSF commander Algoney Dagalo attended a Hague peace conference under the false name "Ahmed Musa" while on a US sanctions list.
RSF's "Tasis" parallel government names ministers, including Dutch-Sudanese lawyer Osama Said as Justice Minister.
